item.title: A four-decadal (1981–2024) quality-assured ground-based soybean phenology dataset from Northeast China: a FAIR-compliant resource for climate impact and agricultural adaptation studies
item.dc:title: A four-decadal (1981–2024) quality-assured ground-based soybean phenology dataset from Northeast China: a FAIR-compliant resource for climate impact and agricultural adaptation studies
item.dc:creator: Quanjun Zhang Dongli Wu a Meteorological Observation Centre, China Meteorological Administration (CMA), Beijing, Chinab State Key Laboratory of Environment Characteristics and Effects for Near-Space, Beijing, Chinac Engineering Technology Research Center for Meteorological Observation of CMA, China Meteorological Administration (CMA), Beijing, ChinaQuanjun Zhang is currently an Associate Researcher at the Meteorological Observation Center of the China Meteorological Administration. As a core research scientist, he has long been dedicated to innovative research in agrometeorological observation theories and technical systems, achieving a series of systematic results in observation network design, automated observation methods, data quality control, and product development. As the first author, he has published over 20 journal papers and holds three granted invention patents together with four utility model patents. Dongli Wu is a professor-level Senior Engineer and Director of the System Department at the Meteorological Observation Center, China Meteorological Administration, where she also serves as Chief Scientist of an innovation team. Her research focuses on agricultural and ecological meteorological observation technologies, specializing in the development of automated systems for monitoring soil moisture, vegetation dynamics, and evapotranspiration. She has led or participated in multiple national research projects, including those under the National Key R&D Program and the National Natural Science Foundation of China. Dr. Wu has authored over 70 scientific publications and contributed to the development of industry standards and observation specifications.
